🎯 The Northwind engagement

Northwind Corporation Ltd is an FMCG company planning to enter the nutrition supplements and protein bar market, starting with the United States and then expanding to other regions. Northwind has hired your company, Litware Inc, an SI partner, to run its market intelligence project. You are Litware's market intelligence consultant, and you will use Copilot Cowork to deliver the engagement end to end.

Whose voice? You build as Litware Inc, the SI partner, but everything you create (prompts, Skills, plugins and apps) runs in Northwind's Microsoft 365 environment and is used by Northwind's own teams. That is why every prompt and skill is written in Northwind's voice, with no reference to Litware.
LabEngagement milestoneWhat you useWhat Northwind gets
Lab 0Scan the US entry marketA detailed Cowork promptA cited US market intelligence report
Lab 1Make intelligence repeatable for expansion markets (UK)A ready-made SkillA consistent weekly brief
Lab 2Test the economics of the US e-commerce launchA plugin: skill + public MCP connector, built with WIQDOne channel profitability recommendation
Lab 3Track market entry across marketsA Cowork app buildAn interactive Market Entry Monitor
How to use this guide: Work through the labs in order. Tick Done on each step to track your progress; it is saved in this browser.
Note: Northwind Corporation Ltd, Litware Inc, Northwind's products and all app demo data are fictional. Market research in Labs 0 and 1 comes from live web sources, and the Lab 2 calculations come from the public Seller Profit Doctor MCP server.
Lab 0

🔎 Lab 0 · Getting started: scan the US market

Northwind's first ask: what does the US protein bar and nutrition supplements market look like, who are the competitor brands, and should we enter? You answer it with a single, detailed natural-language prompt in Cowork, with no Skill or plugin.

5–10 minutesBeginnerNo custom Skill or Plugin
1

Open Cowork and start a new task

Everything in Labs 0, 1 and 3 happens in Copilot Cowork in your browser.

  1. Sign in to Microsoft 365 Copilot using your lab account.
  2. Open Cowork → New task.
What to expect: An empty Cowork task is ready for your prompt.
2

Run the US market scan

The prompt is written as a Northwind market intelligence analyst, because Northwind's own team will reuse it. It sets the company, the market and the exact report structure Northwind leadership needs.

Copy the prompt below and submit it. Review the plan if it is displayed, and respond to any approvals or clarifications.

Prompt
I am a Market Intelligence Analyst at Northwind Corporation Ltd, an FMCG company planning to enter the nutrition supplements and protein bar market, starting with the United States before expanding to other regions. Prepare a structured market intelligence report for Northwind leadership covering: (1) US protein bar and nutrition supplements market overview (size, growth, key consumer segments and sales channels), (2) five relevant competitor brands, (3) emerging opportunities for Northwind, (4) market-entry risks, including regulatory and labelling considerations, and (5) recommendations for Northwind leadership. Cite important claims and distinguish verified facts from assumptions.
Be patient: It can take up to 7 minutes for Cowork to complete the market research and generate the report.
What to expect: Cowork researches the web and returns a structured US market intelligence report.
3

Review the report and its sources

Before the report goes to Northwind leadership, check that the content is complete and the claims are sourced.

  • Market overview and five competitor brands
  • Opportunities, risks and recommendations
  • Source citations or explicitly stated research gaps
Reflect: What if Northwind's own team needs this report for the next expansion markets every week, in the same format, without rewriting a detailed prompt? That is Lab 1.
View reference output

Example of a market intelligence report produced in Cowork for Lab 0. Your report may differ depending on the sources available and when you run the task.

Generate this week's brief for the UK

View reference output

Example of the UK weekly Market Intelligence Brief generated using the Skill. Review the report and its sources; your output may vary depending on the reporting window and available information.

Completion Check

Before moving to the next lab, review your Market Intelligence Brief against the following completion criteria.

  • Skill added in Cowork; geography question answered
  • News summary, trends, competitor analysis, implications and recommendations
Key takeaway: Lab 0 researched the US entry market with a detailed prompt. Lab 1 applies the same methodology to the United Kingdom with a short request. A short prompt does not replace reliable source data.
Lab 2

🛒 Lab 2 · Plugins & MCP: US e-commerce launch economics

Scenario. Your market intelligence work for Northwind Corporation Ltd shows that e-commerce is the fastest, lowest-cost way to test US demand for protein bars before a national retail rollout. Northwind has soft-launched a 12-bar multipack on its own Shopify DTC store, and its e-commerce team wants Cowork to answer: Should we add Amazon? Is a launch discount worth it? Are our social ads paying back? Your Litware team builds the plugin that lets them ask it.

Beginner friendlyPowerShell 7WIQDPublic MCP

🎯 What we will build

A small Cowork plugin built with WIQD. It has a skill that tells Cowork how to think about Northwind's channel profitability, and a connector to the public Seller Profit Doctor MCP server, which provides ready-made calculators for Amazon and Shopify fees, Amazon FBA, launch discounts and ad break-even. There is nothing to host. At the end, Cowork turns Northwind's launch question into one recommendation.

Lab flow: Prerequisites → Create plugin → Add skill → Add MCP connector → Provision & package → Cowork (test)

Whose voice? You build as Litware Inc, the SI partner, but everything you create (prompts, Skills, plugins and apps) runs in Northwind's Microsoft 365 environment and is used by Northwind's own teams. That is why every prompt and skill is written in Northwind's voice, with no reference to Litware.
Stuck while building? A ready-made plugin package is available as a backup in step 22, so you can still complete the Cowork test.
Lab 2 · Setup

⚙️ Prerequisites

Configure your machine. Install or verify every tool before starting the lab.

7

Open PowerShell as Administrator

All commands in this lab run from PowerShell. Administrator mode avoids permission issues while installing tools and creating folders.

  1. Select Start and type PowerShell.
  2. Right-click Windows PowerShell and select Run as administrator.
  3. Select Yes in the User Account Control prompt.
What to expect: A PowerShell window opens with Administrator in the title bar.
8

Verify PowerShell version (7 or later)

WIQD requires PowerShell version 7 or later. Older Windows PowerShell (5.1) can cause commands to fail.

Verify that your PowerShell version is 7 or later:

PowerShell
pwsh --version
What to expect: The output shows PowerShell 7.x.x.

If pwsh is not recognized, install the latest PowerShell (version 7 or later):

PowerShell
winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget

After installation, search for PowerShell from Start and verify again:

PowerShell
pwsh --version
Important: The version verification is only needed here. From step 11 onward, you will use a normal PowerShell window (not as Administrator).
9

Verify Node.js and npm

WIQD runs on Node.js, so Node.js and npm must be installed.

PowerShell
node --version
PowerShell
npm --version
What to expect: Both commands return a version number (your version may be newer).

If either command is not recognized, install Node.js LTS, then close and reopen Windows PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell
winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e
10

Verify Work IQ Dev Tools (WIQD)

WIQD creates, configures, provisions, and packages the Cowork plugin.

PowerShell
wiqd --version
What to expect: A version number is returned.

If WIQD is not recognized, install it, then reopen Windows PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell
iex "& { $(irm 'https://aka.ms/wiqd/install.ps1') }"

Markdown
---
name: channel-profit-analysis
description: Analyze e-commerce channel profitability for Northwind Corporation Ltd's US protein bar and nutrition supplement launch, including Amazon and Shopify fees, Amazon FBA costs, launch discounts, advertising break-even, shipping and packaging costs, and margins.
---

# Northwind Channel Profit Analysis

You support Northwind Corporation Ltd's e-commerce and commercial teams. Northwind is an FMCG company entering the nutrition supplements and protein bar market (United States first, then other regions) and is testing US demand through e-commerce (its own Shopify DTC store and, potentially, Amazon) before scaling into national retail.

Help Northwind leadership understand the financial impact of channel choice, pricing, marketplace fees, launch discounts, fulfillment, shipping, advertising and product costs.

Use the available Seller Profit Doctor tools when the user asks about:

- Amazon or Shopify fees on a protein bar or supplement SKU
- Amazon FBA fees and fulfillment options
- Profit or margin per pack or order
- Channel comparisons (Amazon vs Shopify DTC)
- Launch discounts, coupons and trial promotions
- Advertising break-even
- ROAS
- Shipping and packaging costs
- Launch pricing decisions
- Launch profitability

## Core instructions

1. Understand Northwind's launch objective (for example trial, sales velocity, margin or channel learning) before selecting a tool.
2. Break broad business questions into relevant profitability questions.
3. Determine which available tools can provide evidence for each question.
4. Use multiple tools when necessary instead of relying on one calculation.
5. Use the user's actual numbers whenever they are provided.
6. Never invent missing prices, landed costs, fees, pack sizes, order volumes, shipping costs or advertising spend.
7. Ask only for information that is essential to completing the analysis.
8. Clearly distinguish revenue, channel fees, fulfillment costs, product cost and profit.
9. Explain what the calculated numbers mean in simple business language for Northwind leadership.
10. Identify the important trade-offs between different options.
11. Clearly state assumptions and defaults used by the tools, such as the Amazon category, the FBA size and weight band, and the Shopify plan.
12. Treat calculations as estimates based on the information and rates returned by the tools.
13. Northwind does not sell on Etsy. If a tool also returns an Etsy figure, treat it only as a reference point and do not recommend Etsy as a channel.
14. Do not make health, nutrition or efficacy claims about the products. Focus on the commercial analysis.

## Decision-making guidance

When the user asks a broad business question:

1. Identify the decisions Northwind is trying to make.
2. Break the objective into smaller analytical questions.
3. Select the appropriate tools for each question.
4. Use more than one tool when the decision involves multiple factors.
5. Compare and connect the tool results.
6. Identify risks, opportunities and important trade-offs.
7. Produce one overall recommendation supported by the calculations.
8. Do not merely repeat individual tool outputs.
9. Turn the results into practical, actionable business guidance.
10. Prioritize actions according to their likely effect on launch profitability.

## Relevant considerations

When appropriate, consider:

- Selling price per pack
- Pack format (for example a 12-bar multipack)
- Shipping charged to the customer
- Channel fees (Amazon referral fee, Shopify card fees)
- Amazon category (grocery for protein bars, beauty-health for supplements)
- Amazon FBA fee and the pack's size and weight band
- Landed product cost (co-manufacturing, ingredients, freight)
- Shipping-label cost
- Packaging cost
- Discount percentage
- Current monthly order volume
- Additional orders required
- Advertising spend
- ROAS
- Break-even ROAS
- Profit per order
- Profit margin
- Monthly platform-plan fees
- Channel reach, marketing requirements, consumer data and brand control

## Channel comparisons

When comparing Amazon and Shopify DTC:

1. Compare the fees on an equivalent sale.
2. Consider applicable monthly plan fees.
3. Consider Northwind's expected monthly order volume.
4. Explain that lower transaction fees do not automatically make a channel the best business choice.
5. Consider that Amazon provides marketplace traffic and fast fulfillment, while Shopify DTC gives Northwind first-party consumer data and brand control but needs separate marketing investment.
6. Compare Amazon FBA fees with Northwind's own shipping-label and packaging costs.
7. Clearly identify any assumed Amazon category, plan, fulfillment method or advertising setting.

## Launch discounts

When analyzing a launch promotion or discount:

1. Calculate the financial effect of the discount.
2. Determine the additional orders needed to maintain the original profit.
3. Explain whether the required increase in sales appears realistic for a new brand.
4. Warn the user if the discounted order produces little or no profit.
5. Recommend a smaller discount or another trial-building strategy when appropriate.

## Advertising

When analyzing advertising:

1. Calculate the break-even ROAS for the channel the ads send buyers to.
2. Compare it with any actual ROAS supplied by the user.
3. Explain whether the advertising is generating or losing money.
4. Distinguish advertising-platform attribution from Northwind's actual order data.
5. Avoid recommending additional advertising spend unless the available calculations support it.

## Response style

Keep answers clear, concise and suitable for Northwind leadership.

For broad business questions, structure the response as:

1. Executive recommendation
2. Current position
3. Options analyzed
4. Important calculations
5. Risks and assumptions
6. Recommended next actions, each with a Northwind owner role (for example CMO, CFO or Head of E-commerce)

Use a small comparison table when it improves readability.

Always show the numbers supporting the recommendation.

Do not present the answer as a raw calculator response. Synthesize the available tool results into one decision-oriented recommendation.
View reference output
What to expect: The name in the file matches the folder name: channel-profit-analysis.

          "labelCost"
        ],
        "additionalProperties": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
View reference output
What to expect: toolDescription.json is in the appPackage folder.
16

Save toolDescription.json as UTF-8

Notepad can save the file in a way the package validator rejects. This re-saves it as plain UTF-8.

PowerShell
$json = Get-Content .\appPackage\toolDescription.json -Raw
View reference output
PowerShell
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Resolve-Path .\appPackage\toolDescription.json),$json,[System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
View reference output
What to expect: Both commands finish with no output.
17

Add the Seller Profit Doctor connector

The connector links the plugin to the public Seller Profit Doctor MCP server, which provides the e-commerce fee and profitability calculators.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin add connector --name "Seller Profit Doctor" --description "Read-only e-commerce channel profitability tools for Amazon and Shopify" --url "https://sellerprofitdoctor.com/api/mcp" --tool-description ./toolDescription.json
View reference output
What to expect: Added MCP connector "Seller Profit Doctor" with Auth None.

23

Ask Cowork a business question

Instead of naming a tool, give Cowork a goal. It splits the goal into smaller questions, picks the right tools, and joins the results into one recommendation.

Start a new Cowork task and enter this prompt. It is written as Northwind's e-commerce lead, because Northwind's team will ask this kind of question once the plugin is live:

Prompt
I lead e-commerce for Northwind Corporation Ltd's US protein bar launch. We have soft-launched a 12-bar protein bar multipack on our own Shopify DTC store (Basic plan) at $29.99 with free shipping. Each pack has a landed product cost of $10.80, the shipping label costs $6.50 and packaging costs $1.20. The store currently sells about 1,200 packs a month.

Our leadership team is considering three options before scaling the launch: (1) also selling on Amazon with FBA in the Grocery category (the pack ships in a standard box weighing 1-2 lb), (2) a 20% launch discount on Shopify to drive trial, and (3) continuing to spend $6,000 a month on Facebook and Instagram ads to the Shopify store, which Meta reports at a ROAS of 2.4.

Act as our channel profitability advisor. Analyze our current position and these options. Use the available seller tools where relevant, connect the findings, identify the important trade-offs, and recommend how we should launch to protect margin while building trial.

Show the calculations supporting your recommendation, clearly state any assumptions, and give a prioritized action plan with owners from our leadership team. Do not treat each calculation as a separate answer. Give one overall business recommendation.
View reference output
View reference output
Note: These tools only calculate and change nothing, so Cowork runs them without asking for approval.
What to expect: One recommendation for Northwind covering current Shopify DTC profit per pack, adding Amazon FBA, the 20% launch discount and the $6,000 monthly ad budget, with the numbers, assumptions and a prioritized action plan with Northwind owners.
🎉
Great, you finished Lab 2!
Cowork used your skill and a public MCP connector to turn Northwind's launch question into one clear recommendation.
Lab 3

📊 Lab 3 · Build Northwind's Market Entry Monitor app

Northwind leadership wants more than reports. Your Litware team builds a simple app in Northwind's environment that leadership can use to track protein bar and nutrition supplement market developments across the US, Canada, the UK and Australia as they plan their market-entry sequence, and to follow up on the recommended actions from the briefs and channel analysis.

15–20 minutesIntermediateNo codeDemo data, saved in your browser
24

Build the app from one prompt

One detailed prompt with clear build rules produces a working single-page app.

Go to Cowork → New task, then copy the prompt below and submit it.

Prompt
Build a single-page "Protein & Nutrition Market Entry Monitor" app for
Northwind Corporation Ltd (an FMCG company) leadership to track nutrition
supplement and protein bar market developments across geographies.

TABS:
1. Dashboard: 4 headline counts (trends, competitor moves, high-impact risks,
   open actions), one bar chart of records by geography, and lists of
   opportunities and risks.
2. Intelligence: one searchable list of competitor brands, trends, opportunities
   and risks, each showing geography, confidence (High/Medium/Low) and impact.
3. Action Tracker: a table of recommended actions where I can change priority,
   owner, due date and status (Not started / In progress / Blocked / Completed).
4. Add Intelligence: a form to add or edit a record, plus a field to add a new
   geography.

A geography filter and a search box at the top apply to every tab.

DEMO DATA: realistic made-up data on the protein bar and nutrition supplement
category for United States, Canada, UK and Australia. For each geography:
3 competitor brands (fictional names), 3 trends, 2 opportunities, 2 risks and
3 recommended actions, all in a single reporting period (Q4 2026).

All changes must save in the browser and still be there after a page refresh.

BUILD RULES (follow exactly):
- Build immediately. Do not ask me any questions; use sensible defaults.
- Store all data in browser localStorage only. Do not use SharePoint, Dataverse,
  Fabric, connectors, external APIs or AI features, and do not offer to save the
  data anywhere else. Keep it local.
- One page only, with 4 tabs. No extra pages or routes.
- Keep the code compact: one data file and one page file.
- Do not publish the app yet.
Be patient: It can take 5–7 minutes for the app to finish setting up and open in the live preview.
What to expect: The app opens in the live preview with four tabs: Dashboard, Intelligence, Action Tracker and Add Intelligence.
25

Explore the dashboard, filter and search

Check that leadership can slice the intelligence by market and topic.

  1. On Dashboard, review the four headline counts, the bar chart by geography, and the opportunity and risk lists.
  2. Set the geography filter to United Kingdom, then type pricing in the search box.
  3. Move between tabs and confirm the filter and search apply to every tab. Then clear both.
What to expect: The Intelligence list shows geography, confidence and impact for each record, and the filter and search apply on every tab.
26

Update actions and add a new market

Northwind will keep adding markets as it expands beyond the US, so the app must be editable.

  1. On Action Tracker, change the status of one action to Blocked and change its owner.
  2. On Add Intelligence, add the geography Germany, then add one new trend for it.
  3. Refresh the preview and confirm your changes are still there.
What to expect: Priority, owner, due date and status can be changed, and all changes survive a refresh.
27

Publish and share the app with Northwind

Publishing turns the preview into an app that Northwind leadership can open.

  1. In the same Cowork task, send Publish the app. Approve the request if prompted, then open the app link that Cowork returns.
  2. In the same task, send Share the app with user.diqjf1q7@copilotstudiotraining.onmicrosoft.com. Approve the sharing request if prompted.
What to expect: Cowork reports the app as published and shared.
Key takeaway: Labs 0 and 1 turn research into reports, Lab 2 turns numbers into a decision, and Lab 3 turns the same Northwind scenario into a working tool that leadership can filter, search and update. All app data is fictional demo data saved only in your browser.
